questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Academic opportunities

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: The university with a department of Jewish Studies - something that is not possible in a Scandinavian context and is generally very limited within Europe. Furthermore, the aspect of language was crucial. Being in Montréal allowed me to study at an anglophone university with native English speakers, all the while learning French by exposure and by a course.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: McGill has an learning environment which has been truly inspiring for me and my further studies. They have professors and classes of high quality and their engagement between the different studies and extracurricular conferences were incredible to partake.

questions.question: How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: There was quite a lot of information upon arriving, both with choosing courses, but also certain tests that had to be taken in advance. It wasn't impossible, at all, but it did require a lot of time to navigate.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: They had different introductory events for exchange students which I found to be useful for practical information, but I did not partake in the social events (simply out of personal preference).

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
questions.answer: Generally they were available and it was easy to find.

questions.question: How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: It was fairly easy for me, I used local facebook groups and my own personal network.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: It can take a moment to find, but I think it was really nice to become engaged in a local community rather than solely a university community.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I didn't have student specific housing, so I do not know.

questions.question: How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Confusing, but not at all impossible. Everyone chooses simultaneously and it feels stressful. However, you have a final registration the first week of the semester, meaning you can try courses and drop the ones that are not for you. This meant that I only got professors of great quality.

questions.question: Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: A lot of time spent navigating the website, figuring out what is up and down. It took a while, just like it would at any university, to be frank. However, the language courses, specifically FRSL-courses, were confusing to register to.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: I e-mailed some professors directly who were available to answer questions.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: Full success.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Spent some time looking at the curriculum, google the professors.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: It was of very high quality, but on the undergrad, students aren't treated like adults as in Scandinavia.

questions.question: Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA classes while you were on exchange *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: I think, as is the case in North America generally, that the expectations of some professors to undergrad students were lower because people start younger. I didn't enjoy this aspect, but then I received extra work/different tasks when I asked for it.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: There are more classes and a lot more contact with the professors., including office hours. There is, as previously stated, less focus on critical and independent thinking and more on the comprehension and extraction from the different materials.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
JWST 199 FYS:Images-Jewish Identities

JWST 240 The Holocaust

FRSL 212 Oral & Written French 1

JWST 245 Jewish Life - Islamic World

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: All of the above. Especially the ones with Prof. Christopher Silver. He's very inspiring, concise, intelligent and curious. He is genuinely interested in his field and expects a lot from you.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: Finding a bed because my room was unfurnished. Finding warmer clothes was also necessary.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: I was very lucky to find a cheap room.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I joined a wonderful chamber choir.

questions.question: What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Music and a critical film club.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Join a music ensemble, go apple picking.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Organize a hiking trip, go to a festival, etc.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Very easy, people a kind and hospitable.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Be kind and say hi.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: None. But everyone mixes up the Netherlands and Denmark.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: The warm, hospitable, inviting and smiling way to interact with each other.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
Engage in the local communities outside the university. 

Be prepared to study and do a lot of small assignments. 

Be prepared to meet sweet people.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: Find other exchange students to figure out the RAMQ- things.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: The people I met, the local friends, the music scene, the inspiring university life, the courses and the wonderful energies present.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: The cold, brrrr. :(

questions.question: Any other comments?
questions.answer: The cold is all worth it. Montréal is very bike-friendly, but get a helmet and give up when it gets icy.

questions.question: Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
